## Tutorials

The LAST_DAY() function extracts the last day of the month for a given date.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LAST_DAY("2017-06-20");

---

LAST_DAY(
date
)

---

SELECT LAST_DAY("2017-02-10 09:34:00");
```

## Tutorials

The LOCALTIME() function returns the current date and time.

Note:The date and time is returned as "YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS" 
(string) or as YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.uuuuuu (numeric).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT 
  LOCALTIME();

---

LOCALTIME()

---

SELECT 
  LOCALTIME() + 1;
```

## Tutorials

The LOCALTIMESTAMP() function returns the current date and time.

Note:The date and time is returned as "YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS" 
(string) or as YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.uuuuuu (numeric).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT 
  LOCALTIMESTAMP();

---

LOCALTIMESTAMP()

---

SELECT 
  LOCALTIMESTAMP() + 1;
```

## Tutorials

The MAKEDATE() function creates and returns a date based on a year and a 
number of days value.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT MAKEDATE(2017, 3);

---

MAKEDATE(
year
,
day
)

---

SELECT MAKEDATE(2017, 175);

---

SELECT MAKEDATE(2017, 100);

---

SELECT MAKEDATE(2017, 366);
```

## Tutorials

The MAKETIME() function creates and returns a time based on an hour, minute, 
and second value.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT MAKETIME(11, 35, 
  4);

---

MAKETIME(
hour
,
minute
,
second
)

---

SELECT MAKETIME(16, 
  1, 0);

---

SELECT MAKETIME(21, 
  59, 59);

---

SELECT MAKETIME(838, 
  59, 59);
```
